overview: Jordan is a country in Western Asia, east of the Jordan River. Its capital and largest city is Amman. Jordan is a kingdom and became independent from British administration in 1946. It is home to Petra, an ancient city carved into rose-coloured rock, and it has taken in large numbers of refugees from neighbouring countries.

geography.text: Most of Jordan is desert, including the dramatic valley of Wadi Rum in the south. In the west, the Jordan Rift Valley runs down to the Dead Sea, the lowest point on land. Jordan's only coast is a short stretch on the Gulf of Aqaba, an arm of the Red Sea.

history.text: Jordan's history includes the Nabataeans, who carved the city of Petra, and Roman cities such as Jerash. After Ottoman rule, Britain created the Emirate of Transjordan in 1921, which became independent as the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in 1946. Jordan has taken in many refugees from conflicts in neighbouring countries and made peace with Israel in 1994.

events.title: Petra
events.text: The Nabataeans make Petra their capital.

events.title: Transjordan
events.text: Britain creates the Emirate of Transjordan.

events.title: West Bank lost
events.text: Israel takes the West Bank in the Six-Day War.

events.title: Peace with Israel
events.text: Jordan and Israel sign a peace treaty.

government.text: Jordan is a constitutional monarchy. The King, from the Hashemite family, holds wide powers: he appoints the Prime Minister and can dissolve parliament. Parliament has an elected House of Representatives and a Senate appointed by the King.

economy.text: Jordan has few natural resources and little water. Its economy relies on services, tourism, phosphates and potash, and aid from abroad. It has taken in large numbers of refugees from Palestine, Iraq and Syria.

culture.text: Petra, a city carved into rose-red rock by the Nabataeans, is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. The desert of Wadi Rum has been used as a film location for Mars. Mansaf, lamb cooked in fermented yoghurt, is the national dish and on UNESCO's heritage list.

items.title: Petra
items.text: A city cut into sandstone cliffs more than 2,000 years ago.

items.title: Wadi Rum
items.text: A desert valley used to film movies set on Mars.

items.title: Mansaf
items.text: Lamb and rice with yoghurt sauce, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Jordan reached the final of the Asian Cup in 2024 and qualified for its first World Cup in 2026. Taekwondo has brought Olympic gold.

items.title: Ahmad Abughaush
items.text: Won Jordan's first Olympic gold, in taekwondo, in 2016.
